title: Finalytics data types
description: The types exchanged between the Finalytics engine and its Python and JavaScript bindings.

lot_method.description: How sales in this account choose lots, unless a sale says otherwise.

Account.description: An account in a portfolio, such as a brokerage or custody account.

AccountId.description:
Identifies an account within a portfolio.

Identifiers are non-empty, have no leading or trailing whitespace, and are compared
exactly (case matters).

oneOf.description: `amount` (in `currency`) moved into `holding` (negative: out of it).

amount.description: The amount, net of tax withheld.

oneOf.description: `amount` (in `currency`) earned by `holding` and paid out to cash, such as a dividend.

from.description: The instrument given up, wholly or in part.

oneOf.description:
`quantity` units of `to` replaced part of `from` (a spin-off, merger or symbol change);
the value moved is the market value of the new units on the date.

Allocation.description:
How a transaction moved value between holdings, used to measure each holding's
contribution. Value moved between holdings nets to zero; only external flows change the
portfolio's total.

AssetBound.description: Limits on one asset's weight, in place of the default bounds.

min.description: The smallest weight allowed; negative for a short position.

Bound.description: Lower and upper limits on a weight.

CashBalance.description: A cash balance in one account and currency.

fx_rate.description: Units of base currency per unit of `currency`.

value_base.description: The balance in the base currency.

CashValue.description: A cash balance valued on a date.

budget.description: The sum of the weights; 1 by default.

bounds.description: Bounds on every weight; `[0, 1]` by default.

asset_bounds.description: Bounds on particular assets, in place of `bounds`.

leverage.description: The largest gross exposure, `sum |w|`, for portfolios with short positions.

turnover.description: A turnover limit and trading costs.

Constraints.description: The constraints on a portfolio. The default is fully invested and long-only.

contribution.description:
Its contribution to the portfolio's time-weighted return. Contributions of all holdings
add up to the portfolio's return over the period.

return_base.description: The holding's own return in the base currency, when it can be measured.

return_local.description: The holding's own return in its own currency, when it can be measured.

currency_effect.description: `return_base - return_local`: what currency movements added or took away.

average_weight.description: The holding's average share of the portfolio's value at the end of each day.

Contribution.description: What one holding added to the portfolio's return over a period.

matrix.description:
The covariance matrix, labelled like the returns. Scale it to annualise, for example
with `Matrix::scaled` by 252 for daily returns.

shrinkage.description: The shrinkage intensity, between 0 and 1, for the shrinkage estimators.

observations.description: The number of returns per asset used.

CovarianceEstimate.description: An estimated covariance matrix, per period of the returns.

oneOf.description: The sample covariance, with divisor n - 1.

An exponentially weighted covariance: the return `k` periods before the latest has
weight proportional to `decay^k`, the weights sum to one, and deviations are taken from
the weighted mean. A decay of 0.94 for daily returns follows RiskMetrics.

The empirical covariance (divisor n) shrunk towards a multiple of the identity with the
intensity of Ledoit and Wolf (2004).

The empirical covariance (divisor n) shrunk towards a multiple of the identity with the
oracle approximating shrinkage intensity of Chen, Wiesel, Eldar and Hero (2010).

CovarianceMethod.description: How a covariance matrix is estimated from returns.

Currency.description: An ISO 4217 currency code, for example "USD".

Date.description: A calendar date in ISO 8601 form, for example "2026-11-02".

Decimal.description: An exact decimal number. Finalytics writes decimals as strings, such as "201.50", and reads strings or numbers.

quote.description: The currency it is priced in.

DocumentFxRates.description: The rates for one currency pair in a portfolio document.

pivot.description: The currency through which FX rates are crossed; USD by default.

max_carry_days.description: How many days a price or rate may be carried forward; 5 by default.

prices.description: Prices by instrument, in each instrument's currency.

fx.description: FX rates: units of `quote` per unit of `base`.

DocumentMarketData.description: Market data stored in a portfolio document.

peak.description: The date of the peak the fall started from.

trough.description: The date of the lowest point.

recovery.description: The first date at or above the peak again, or `None` if the series has not recovered.

depth.description: The fall from the peak to the trough, as a negative return (-0.25 for a fall of 25%).

days_to_trough.description: Calendar days from the peak to the trough.

days_to_recovery.description: Calendar days from the trough to the recovery, if it happened.

Drawdown.description: One fall from a peak, to the trough and, if it happened, back to the peak.

oneOf.description: A lot was opened or changed; this is its new state.
A lot was closed.
Cash in one currency changed by `amount` (negative for a payment).

Effect.description: A change to the books made by one transaction.

index.description: Its position in the portfolio's transaction list.

allocations.description: How it moved value between holdings.

Event.description: One transaction as applied to the books.

ExcessReturn.description: A return compared with a benchmark's over the same dates.

amount.description: The value, positive into the portfolio.

kind.description: What kind of flow it was.

Flow.description: Value entering (positive) or leaving (negative) the portfolio, in `currency`.

oneOf.description: Cash deposited.
Cash withdrawn.
Units transferred in, at market value.
Units transferred out, at market value.

FlowKind.description:
Why value entered or left the portfolio from outside: the flows that performance measurement
must separate from investment returns.

oneOf.description: At the start of the day: a deposit earns that day's return.
At the end of the day: a deposit starts earning the next day.

FlowTiming.description: When external flows are assumed to happen within the day they are recorded on.

FrontierPoint.description: A portfolio on the efficient frontier.

contribution.description: The sum of its holdings' contributions.

average_weight.description: The sum of its holdings' average weights.

GroupContribution.description: What a group of holdings (an asset class, a region) added to the portfolio's return.

name.description: The group's name, used in messages.

assets.description: The labels of the assets in the group.

GroupLimit.description: Limits on the total weight of a group of assets, such as an asset class or a region.

weight.description: The sum of its assets' weights.

component.description: The sum of its assets' components.

share.description: The sum of its assets' shares, `None` when the portfolio has no volatility.

GroupRisk.description: A group's share of a portfolio's volatility.

oneOf.description: An instrument.
Cash in one currency.

HoldingKey.description:
A holding for performance attribution: an instrument, or cash in one currency, added up
across accounts.

currency.description: The holding's own currency: the instrument's, or the cash currency.

values_local.description: The value at the end of each date, in `currency`.

values_base.description: The value at the end of each date, in the base currency.

trades_local.description: The value moved in since the previous date, in `currency`.

trades_base.description: The value moved in since the previous date, in the base currency.

income_local.description: The income earned since the previous date, in `currency`.

income_base.description: The income earned since the previous date, in the base currency.

HoldingLine.description:
One holding's values, trades and income on each date of a `HoldingSeries`.

Trades and income are those since the previous date. Value moved between holdings (a
purchase moves cash into a share) appears as a trade out of one line and into another, so
trades across all lines add up to the portfolio's external flows plus its income.

holdings.description: The holdings, in the order of the table's columns.

dates.description: The date each return ends on: every date given but the first.

table.description:
The returns, one column per holding, labelled with the instrument identifier or, for
cash, the currency code followed by " cash".

warnings.description: Prices and rates carried forward from earlier dates.

HoldingReturns.description: Returns of holdings in the base currency between consecutive dates.

lines.description: One line per instrument and per cash currency held at any time, in key order.

warnings.description: Prices and rates carried forward from earlier dates.

HoldingSeries.description:
Values, value moved in and income per holding over dates, in the holding's currency and in
the base currency: the input to contribution analysis.

currency.description: The currency it is priced and traded in.

multiplier.description:
The value of one unit at a price of one: 1 for shares, the contract size for futures
and options.

classifications.description: Classifications by scheme, for example `asset_class: Equity`, `region: Europe`.

identifiers.description: Other identifiers by scheme, for example `isin` or `ticker`.

Instrument.description: Something a portfolio can hold, other than cash.

InstrumentId.description:
Identifies an instrument, for example `"AAPL"` or `"US0378331005"`.

Identifiers are non-empty, have no leading or trailing whitespace, and are compared
exactly (case matters).

oneOf.description: A share in a company.
A mutual fund, exchange-traded fund or similar pooled vehicle.
A bond, priced per unit (supply clean or dirty prices consistently).
A futures contract, priced per unit of the underlying with a contract multiplier.
An option, priced per unit of the underlying with a contract multiplier.
An FX forward, priced as its value per unit of notional.
Anything else.

InstrumentKind.description:
What kind of instrument something is.

Every kind is held and valued the same way, as a quantity times a price times a multiplier.
Derivatives and bonds are supplied already priced; Finalytics does not price them.

path.description: Where the problem is, for example `transactions[14].quantity`.

message.description: What is wrong, in plain words.

Issue.description: One problem found while validating input.

oneOf.description: The distance between the closest members (the method of López de Prado, 2016).
The distance between the furthest members.
The mean distance between members.
The increase in within-cluster variance (Ward's method).

Linkage.description: How clusters are joined in hierarchical risk parity.

quantity.description: The remaining quantity, greater than zero while the lot is open.

cost_local.description: The remaining cost basis in the instrument's currency, including acquisition fees.

cost_base.description: The remaining cost basis in the base currency.

acquired.description: The acquisition date, which sets the holding period.

opened_by.description:
The transaction that opened the lot (or the earliest one, for lots carried through
corporate actions).

sequence.description: The order in which lots were opened, used to break ties.

Lot.description:
Units of one instrument acquired together, with their remaining cost basis.

Costs are totals for the remaining quantity, in the instrument's currency (`cost_local`) and in
the portfolio's base currency at the acquisition rate (`cost_base`). Keeping totals rather than
unit costs means that splitting a lot never loses or creates cost.

LotId.description:
Identifies a tax lot: the transaction that opened it, followed by `/` and the corporate
action that derived it, if any.

Identifiers are non-empty, have no leading or trailing whitespace, and are compared
exactly (case matters).

oneOf.description: First in, first out: the oldest lots first.
Last in, first out: the newest lots first.
The lots with the highest cost per unit first.
The lots with the lowest cost per unit first.
Every lot reduced in proportion, so each sale carries the average cost.
The lots named by the sale.

LotMethod.description: How sales choose which tax lots to close.

quantity.description: The number of units to take from it.

LotPick.description: A lot named by a sale or transfer, for specific identification.

quantity.description: The units the sale would take from it.

cost_local.description: The cost basis of those units in the instrument's currency.

cost_base.description: The cost basis of those units in the base currency.

LotSale.description: The part of a lot that a sale would close.

Matrix.description:
A square matrix with labelled rows and columns, stored row by row; a covariance or
correlation matrix.

oneOf.description: The Clarabel interior-point solver for convex conic programmes.
Newton's method on the convex risk-budgeting problem.
Hierarchical clustering and recursive bisection, without a solver.

Method.description: The method that produced a solution.

Money.description:
An exact decimal amount in one currency.

Arithmetic between amounts checks that the currencies match and that no overflow occurs.
Amounts keep their full precision until `Money::round` is called.

oneOf.description: The smallest variance.

risk_aversion.description: The weight on variance, greater than zero.

oneOf.description: The largest `expected return - risk_aversion / 2 * variance`.
The smallest variance with an expected return of at least `target`.

target.description: The volatility allowed, greater than zero.

oneOf.description: The largest expected return with a volatility of at most `target`.

risk_free_rate.description: The risk-free rate, in the units of the expected returns.

oneOf.description: The largest Sharpe ratio, `(expected return - risk_free_rate) / volatility`.

The largest diversification ratio: the weighted average of the assets' volatilities over
the portfolio's volatility (Choueifaty and Coignard, 2008).

The smallest conditional value at risk (expected shortfall) of the scenario returns, by
the linear programme of Rockafellar and Uryasev (2000).

budgets.description: The risk budgets, one per asset, each greater than zero; they are scaled to sum to one.

oneOf.description:
Weights at which each asset's share of the portfolio's volatility equals its budget
(Spinu, 2013). Without budgets every asset contributes equally (risk parity). Only the
default constraints apply.
From the end of the previous month.
From the end of the previous calendar quarter.
From the end of the previous calendar year.
The `years` years before the as-of date (1, 3, 5 …).
From the first valuation.
From `start` to the as-of date.

Period.description: A reporting period ending on an as-of date.

start.description: The valuation date the period starts from.

end.description: The valuation date it ends on.

cumulative.description: The cumulative return over the period.

annualised.description: The annualised return, given only for periods of a year or more.

PeriodReturn.description: A return over a reporting period.

base_currency.description: The currency results are reported in.

instruments.description: The instruments the transactions refer to.

transactions.description:
The transactions, in any order; they are applied by trade date, and in the order given
within a date.

Portfolio.description:
Everything Finalytics needs to keep a portfolio's books: its base currency, accounts,
instruments and transactions.

format_version.description: The version of the format, 1 for this release.

market.description: Market data stored with the portfolio.

PortfolioDocument.description: A portfolio and, optionally, the market data to value it, in one versioned document.

cost_local.description: The total cost basis in the instrument's currency.

cost_base.description: The total cost basis in the base currency.

Position.description: A position: the open lots of one instrument in one account, added up.

price.description: The price used, per unit, in the instrument's currency.

price_date.description: The date the price was observed (earlier than the valuation date if carried forward).

market_value_local.description: `quantity × price × multiplier`, in the instrument's currency.

fx_rate.description: Units of base currency per unit of the instrument's currency.

market_value_base.description: The market value in the base currency.

cost_local.description: The cost basis in the instrument's currency.

cost_base.description: The cost basis in the base currency.

unrealised_base.description: `market_value_base - cost_base`, which includes the currency effect.

PositionValue.description: A position valued on a date.

covariance.description: The covariance matrix of the assets' returns.

expected_returns.description: The expected return of each asset.

scenarios.description: Scenario returns, one column per asset, for minimum CVaR.

Problem.description:
A portfolio optimisation problem: the assets, estimates of their risk and return, and the
constraints.

The covariance matrix and expected returns should be in the same units, for example both
annualised. Scenario returns, for minimum CVaR, are per period.

quantity.description: The units to trade, greater than zero.

price.description: The price per unit, in the instrument's currency.

value_local.description: `quantity × price × multiplier`, in the instrument's currency.

value_base.description: The value in the base currency.

lots.description: For a sale, the lots it closes.

realised_gain_base.description: For a sale, the gain it would realise in the base currency, before fees.

ProposedTrade.description: A proposed trade in one instrument.

quantity.description: The units disposed of (zero for a return of capital beyond the cost basis).

proceeds_local.description: Proceeds net of fees, in the instrument's currency.

cost_local.description: Cost basis in the instrument's currency.

proceeds_base.description: Proceeds in the base currency, at the disposal date's rate.

cost_base.description: Cost basis in the base currency, at the acquisition rates.

gain_base.description: `proceeds_base - cost_base`, which includes the currency effect.

RealisedGain.description: A gain or loss realised by a sale, a return of capital or a cash merger, for one lot.

date.description: The date of the prices used.

value_base.description: The account's value in the base currency.

conversions.description: Conversions that fund purchases in other currencies and reach the target cash balances.

weights_before.description: Each holding's weight before the trades.

weights_after.description: Each holding's weight after the trades.

turnover.description: The value traded, sales and purchases, as a share of the account's value.

realised_gain_base.description: The gain the sales would realise in the base currency.

warnings.description: Carried prices, a shortfall of cash, and trades left out by rounding.

Rebalance.description: The trades that move an account to target weights, and their effects.

lot_method.description: How sales choose lots; first in, first out by default. Highest cost first defers gains.

whole_units.description: Trade whole units only, rounding each trade towards zero.

minimum_trade.description: Leave out trades worth less than this in the base currency.

active_return.description: The annualised return less the benchmark's annualised return.

tracking_error.description: The annualised standard deviation of the active returns (returns less benchmark returns).

information_ratio.description: The annualised mean active return over the tracking error.

beta.description: The covariance of the returns with the benchmark's over the benchmark's variance.

alpha.description:
The mean return not explained by beta, in excess of the risk-free rate, annualised by
compounding: `(1 + mean(r - rf - beta (b - rf)))^periods_per_year - 1`.

correlation.description: The correlation of the returns with the benchmark's.

RelativeStatistics.description: Statistics of a returns series against a benchmark's returns over the same periods.

ReturnsTable.description: The returns of several assets over the same periods, one column per asset.

label.description: The asset, as labelled in the covariance matrix.

marginal.description:
The change in the portfolio's volatility per unit of weight: `(C w)_i / volatility`.
`None` when the portfolio has no volatility.

component.description: `weight * marginal`. The components add up to the portfolio's volatility.

share.description:
`component / volatility`. The shares add up to one. `None` when the portfolio has no
volatility.

RiskContribution.description: One asset's share of a portfolio's volatility.

volatility.description:
The portfolio's volatility, `sqrt(w' C w)`, in the units of the covariance matrix (scale
the matrix to annualise).

contributions.description: Each asset's contribution, in the order of the covariance matrix.

RiskDecomposition.description: A portfolio's volatility split into each asset's contribution (Euler allocation).

oneOf.description: The input can be used, but the caller should know about this.
The input cannot be used as it is.

Severity.description: How serious a validation issue is.

oneOf.description: A purchase.
A sale.

weights.description: The optimal weights, one per asset, when `SolveStatus::has_solution`.

objective_value.description:
The value of the objective at the weights: the variance for minimum variance and target
return; the utility for mean–variance; the expected return for target volatility; the
Sharpe ratio; the diversification ratio; the CVaR, as a positive loss; for risk budgeting,
the largest difference between an asset's share of risk and its budget. `None` for
hierarchical risk parity, which optimises no objective.

expected_return.description: The expected return at the weights, when expected returns are given.

volatility.description: The volatility at the weights, when a covariance matrix is given.

max_violation.description:
The largest amount by which the weights break a constraint (0 when every constraint
holds exactly).

iterations.description: Iterations of the solver or of Newton's method.

Solution.description:
The result of an optimisation, with what is needed to judge it: the status, the objective,
how closely the constraints hold, and the work done.

oneOf.description: Solved to the solver's full accuracy.

Solved to reduced accuracy; the weights are usable but should be checked against
`Solution::max_violation`.
No portfolio satisfies the constraints.
The objective can be improved without limit; add bounds or a leverage limit.
The solver stopped at its iteration limit.

The solver could not make progress, usually because the inputs are badly scaled or
nearly degenerate.

total_return.description: The compounded return over the whole series.

annualised_return.description: The compound annual growth rate: `(1 + total_return)^(periods_per_year / observations) - 1`.

volatility.description: The annualised standard deviation of the returns (sample, divisor n - 1).

downside_deviation.description:
The annualised root mean square of the shortfalls below the target return, over all
observations.

sharpe_ratio.description:
The mean return in excess of the risk-free rate over its standard deviation, annualised by
the square root of `periods_per_year`.

sortino_ratio.description: The annualised mean return in excess of the target over the downside deviation.

max_drawdown.description:
The largest fall from a peak, as a negative return (-0.25 for a fall of 25%), measured
from a starting value before the first return.

calmar_ratio.description: The annualised return over the size of the maximum drawdown; `None` without a drawdown.

skewness.description: The skewness of the returns (population moments).

excess_kurtosis.description:
The kurtosis of the returns less 3, so that a normal distribution has 0 (population
moments).

Statistics.description:
Statistics of a returns series.

Annualised figures scale by `StatisticsOptions::periods_per_year`. Ratios that divide by a
dispersion are `None` when the returns do not vary.

periods_per_year.description:
Return periods in a year: 252 for daily trading-day returns (the default), 52 for weekly,
12 for monthly.

risk_free_rate.description:
The annual risk-free rate for the Sharpe ratio and alpha. It is converted to a rate per
period by compounding: `(1 + rate)^(1 / periods_per_year) - 1`. The default is 0.

target_return.description:
The annual minimum acceptable return for downside deviation and the Sortino ratio,
converted to a rate per period in the same way. The default is 0.

oneOf.description:
From the observed returns: the quantile with linear interpolation between order
statistics, and the mean of the worst `floor((n - 1) * alpha) + 1` returns.
From a normal distribution with the sample mean and standard deviation.

From the normal quantile adjusted for skewness and excess kurtosis by the Cornish–Fisher
expansion. Expected shortfall integrates the Edgeworth expansion of the density to that
quantile (Boudt, Peterson and Croux, 2008), and is never less than the value at risk.

TailMethod.description: How the tail of the return distribution is estimated.

value_at_risk.description: The loss exceeded with probability `1 - confidence`.

expected_shortfall.description:
The expected loss when the value at risk is exceeded (also called conditional value at
risk).

TailRisk.description:
Value at risk and expected shortfall over one period of the returns.

Both are losses, reported as positive returns: a value at risk of 0.021 at 95% confidence
means that one period in twenty is expected to lose 2.1% or more.

TimeSeries.description:
Values indexed by strictly increasing dates.

Construction checks the ordering, so every `TimeSeries` can be searched by date. A series is
serialised as `{"dates": [...], "values": [...]}`, and deserialising checks it again.

benchmark.description: The benchmark's weights, one per asset.

limit.description:
The largest tracking error allowed, `sqrt((w - b)' C (w - b))`, in the units of the
covariance matrix's volatility.

TrackingErrorLimit.description: A limit on ex-ante tracking error against a benchmark.

id.description: The caller's identifier, unique within the portfolio.

account.description: The account the transaction belongs to.

trade_date.description: The date the transaction takes effect for positions and performance.

settle_date.description: The date cash settles, if different from the trade date.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

price.description: The price per unit, zero or more.

fees.description: Commissions and other costs of the trade, added to the cost basis.

oneOf.description: Buy `quantity` units at `price` per unit, paying `fees` on top.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

price.description: The price per unit, zero or more.

fees.description: Commissions and other costs, deducted from the proceeds.

lot_method.description: Overrides the account's lot method for this sale.

lots.description: The lots to close, for specific identification.

oneOf.description: Sell `quantity` units at `price` per unit, with `fees` deducted from the proceeds.
Cash paid into the account from outside the portfolio.
Cash taken out of the portfolio.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

cost_basis.description:
The total cost basis carried over, in the instrument's currency. When absent, the
market value on the trade date is used.

acquired.description: The original acquisition date, when the holding period carries over.

oneOf.description: Units received from outside the portfolio.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

lot_method.description: Overrides the account's lot method for this transfer.

lots.description: The lots to send, for specific identification.

oneOf.description: Units sent out of the portfolio. No gain is realised.

withholding_tax.description: Tax withheld at source, in the same currency.

oneOf.description: A dividend received in cash.

instrument.description: The instrument that paid it, if any.

withholding_tax.description: Tax withheld at source, in the same currency.

oneOf.description: Interest received in cash, from an instrument or on the cash balance.
A fee not tied to a trade, such as a custody or management fee.
A tax not tied to a trade.
Cash converted from one currency to another.

A share split: every `from` units become `to` units, with cost basis unchanged. A reverse
split has `to` below `from`.

cost_allocation.description: The share of cost basis moved to the new units.

oneOf.description:
A spin-off: holders receive `ratio` units of a new instrument per unit held, and a share
`cost_allocation` (between 0 and 1) of the cost basis moves to the new units.

ratio.description: New units per unit held; zero for an all-cash takeover.

cash_per_unit.description: Cash per unit held, in the held instrument's currency.

oneOf.description:
A merger or acquisition: each unit held becomes `ratio` units of `new_instrument`, plus
`cash_per_unit` in cash, which reduces the cost basis (gains beyond the basis are
realised).
The instrument's identifier changes; lots carry over unchanged.

amount.description: The total amount, in the instrument's currency.

oneOf.description:
A return of capital paid in cash, which reduces the cost basis (amounts beyond the basis
are realised as gains).

Transaction.description:
One event in the life of a portfolio.

Transactions are applied in trade-date order; transactions on the same date are applied in the
order given. Positions are booked on the trade date; the settlement date is recorded for cash
reporting.

TransactionId.description:
Identifies a transaction. Lots opened by a transaction take their identity from it.

Identifiers are non-empty, have no leading or trailing whitespace, and are compared
exactly (case matters).

current.description: The current weights, one per asset.

limit.description:
The largest total of absolute weight changes, `sum |w - current|`; 0.2 allows 20% of the
portfolio to be bought and sold in total.

costs.description:
Costs per unit of weight traded, one per asset, in the units of the expected returns.
They reduce the expected return of objectives that use one.

Turnover.description: Trading from the current portfolio: a limit on turnover, costs per unit traded, or both.

ValidationReport.description:
Every problem found while validating an input, rather than only the first.

Each issue carries a path that locates it in the input, so that a user interface can point
to the exact field.

positions.description: The positions, by account and instrument.

cash.description: The cash balances, by account and currency.

total_base.description: Positions and cash, in the base currency.

warnings.description: Prices and rates carried forward from earlier dates.

Valuation.description: The holdings valued on a date.

values.description: The value of the portfolio at the end of each date.

flows.description:
The external flows since the previous date (deposits and transfers in positive;
withdrawals and transfers out negative), each converted at its own date's rate.

warnings.description: Prices and rates carried forward from earlier dates.

ValueSeries.description: Daily values and external flows in the base currency, the input to performance measurement.
